name: Austria
sources: GDP $165.8bn and population 7.68m: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, series AUT, 1990 (165,811,372,383 and 7,677,850). Same series as the rest of the roster.

Inflation 3.3%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, AUT 1990 = 3.262%. The schilling had been held to the D-mark since 1976 - the Hartwahrungspolitik - and Austrian inflation is essentially German inflation with a small lag.
Policy rate 9.0%: three-month Vienna interbank rate, monthly mean of 1990 = 8.964% (OECD MEI via FRED, IR3TIB01ATM156N).
Revenue 39% of GDP: OECD Revenue Statistics, total tax revenue as a share of GDP, Austria 1990 (about 39.4%). Just above Germany's 0.38.
Gross public debt 56% of GDP: IMF World Economic Outlook GGXWDG_NGDP, AUT 1990 = 56.2%.

Military 1.2% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS (SIPRI), AUT 1990 = 1.196% - the lowest in Western Europe together with Ireland's, which is what permanent neutrality bought when the neutral in question was not a Swiss-style armed camp.

Strength index 6: about 55,000 in the Bundesheer with roughly 200,000 on militia mobilisation, 170 or so tanks, no combat aircraft worth the name until the Draken deliveries of 1988. Indexed at Denmark's 6, well below Switzerland's 14 - the other permanently neutral Alpine state, spending a third more of a larger economy on defence and mobilising three times as many people.

Gross fixed capital formation 25.8% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, AUT 1990. Split into public 3.2% and private 22.6% using the AMECO general-government series, private as residual. CAVEAT: total transcribed, public share entered from reference knowledge of AMECO.

Oil 0.02 mbd: Austrian crude production from the Vienna Basin fields ran around 20,000 barrels a day in 1990 - real, small, and entered rather than rounded to zero because OMV was a state oil company of some consequence in central Europe.

Stability 80 and authoritarianism 0.12: at Germany's 80. The SPO-OVP grand coalition of 1986 was the fourth of its kind and the Proporz system had shared out every public appointment in the country between the two of them since 1945. Authoritarianism above Germany's 0.10 and at France's 0.12, because that same Proporz meant a state broadcaster, nationalised industries and a chamber system all allocated by party card rather than by competition. The Waldheim affair - the president elected in 1986 whose wartime service the World Jewish Congress had documented, and who was barred from entering the United States from April 1987 - was live throughout, and it is the reason this is 80 rather than the 85 the machinery would otherwise earn.
Separatism 0.02: below France's 0.03. Slovene and Croat minority-language questions in Carinthia and Burgenland are constitutional and quiet.

TFP trend 0.015: just below Germany's 0.016, and above Spain's 0.009. Austria spent the 1990s converging on German productivity levels from a little below, joined the European Union on 1 January 1995, and got a second, larger dividend nobody had planned for when the border with Hungary and Czechoslovakia opened and Vienna became a regional centre again for the first time since 1918.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.1533%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series AUT (Austria): 7,561,434 in 1984 to 7,619,567 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

reserves_bn = 16.882 ($bn). Total reserves including gold, AUT, 1989: US$16881871851.29 (World Bank World Development Indicators series FI.RES.TOTL.CD, 'Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)', retrieved from the World Bank API on 2026-09-02; indicator lastupdated 2026-07-13). THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. LIMIT STATED: this series is official reserve assets. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: AUT.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 90% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 50721 against a threshold of any positive count: comm_cellular_analogue GRANTED.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS 'Mobile cellular subscriptions', retrieved from the World Bank indicator API (api.worldbank.org/v2), source id 2, lastupdated 2026-07-13. Series values: AUT, 1989 = 50721 subscriptions and 1990 = 73698 subscriptions. The series is a YEAR-END STOCK, so the 1989 figure describes 31 December 1989, i.e. the game's start instant of 1 January 1990: a network was carrying paying subscribers before the start date. All cellular in service at that date was analogue (NMT, AMPS, TACS, C-Netz, RTMS); GSM had no commercial service anywhere until mid-1991.

WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: AUT, 1990 = 90%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name.
